chapters.title: First Wonders
chapters.description: The oldest layer we can glimpse: transformations, sacred fires, and powers remembered more like folktale than history.
chapters.sequenceNote: These stories occupy the deep mythic past; their order inside the era remains deliberately provisional.

chapters.title: Wandering Magic & First Kingdoms
chapters.description: Magic travels in bodies, names, monsters, guests, and village bargains before durable states learn to contain it.
chapters.sequenceNote: A broad early-age sequence inferred from social scale and magical custom, not a dated dynasty list.

chapters.title: Crowns, Covenants & Dragon States
chapters.description: Courts, priesthoods, infernal treaties, hidden heirs, and sleeping dragons turn personal power into political order.
chapters.sequenceNote: The era is secure as a civilizational layer; most story-to-story ordering inside it is still speculative.

chapters.title: Guilds, Colleges & Civic Arcana
chapters.description: Healers measure, schools classify, cities regulate, and ordinary lives grow around magic sturdy enough to become infrastructure.
chapters.sequenceNote: Placed after the crown age by institutional maturity; the individual sequence is a working reconstruction.

chapters.title: Arcane Industry
chapters.description: Foundations, warranties, command structures, and manufactured companions mark a world trying to make magic repeatable.
chapters.sequenceNote: One relationship fixes a local link; the rest follow a speculative rise in technological and civic complexity.

chapters.title: Fallen Engines & Salvage
chapters.description: Vast machines fall, patient rooms wait, names survive wreckage, and the remnants of one high order become another age's ruins.
chapters.sequenceNote: A decline-and-recovery layer inferred from scale, debris, and the way surviving systems are encountered.

chapters.title: The Modern-like Low-Magic Trough
chapters.description: Buses, cafés, clinics, schools, rentals, and small towns dominate the surface while old powers persist in families, mirrors, sleep, weather, and thresholds.
chapters.sequenceNote: Seven stories are fixed to this era by universe authority, but their relative order remains unresolved; neighboring placements use shared material culture and low public magical visibility.

chapters.eyebrow: Not safely reducible to one line
chapters.title: Off-Axis Realms
chapters.description: Some stories cross realms, compress unequal clocks, or sit outside ordinary material time. Their internal sequences are real even when their attachment point is not.
chapters.sequenceNote: Shown beside the trough because of visible modern bridges, without pretending that this settles their universal position.

constellations.title: Ravel / Modern Bridge
constellations.description: A small moon, eleven seconds, four months, and a year belong to the same causal chain but not the same clock.
constellations.sequenceNote: The bridge is explicit; Ravel's position relative to the main material chronology is unresolved.

constellations.title: Modern Frame, Unknown Destinations
constellations.description: A recognizable apartment doorway brackets journeys whose worlds cannot be assigned to the main historical line.
constellations.sequenceNote: Its frame resembles the low-magic present; its ten worlds remain off-axis.

constellations.title: Unresolved Crossings
constellations.description: Realm structure and higher-order play make linear placement less truthful than an open branch.
constellations.sequenceNote: No authoritative hinge currently joins these stories to a material era.

constellations.title: Outside Material Time
constellations.description: A station between worlds belongs to the universe without occupying a stable historical address inside it.
constellations.sequenceNote: Its relation to material eras is intentionally left open.

chapters.title: The Long Reign & the Bay Museum
chapters.description: The Battle of the Bay has passed from lived crisis into curated history—except for the witness still alive to correct the count.
chapters.sequenceNote: Explicitly centuries after Solstice Evening Bell.

chapters.title: Public Return & the Augmented City
chapters.description: Gods, monsters, drones, altered bodies, municipal systems, and engineered mercy share the streets openly.
chapters.sequenceNote: Placed after the trough by visibility and technological integration; most internal ordering remains inferred.

chapters.title: Orbital Zenith & Living Cities
chapters.description: Bodies, clouds, songs, habitats, and watchers stretch civilization from transformed cities into orbit and the outer system.
chapters.sequenceNote: A high-technology sequence inferred from spatial reach and social integration.

chapters.title: Archive Civilizations & Reclaimed Worlds
chapters.description: Kingdoms, foundations, and starward rituals persist long enough to be buried, excavated, reconstructed, and misunderstood by successor cultures.
chapters.sequenceNote: A far-future layer inferred from deep-time archaeology and civilizational refounding.

chapters.title: The Glass-Sea Catastrophe
chapters.description: The Day of Glass consumes six outer cities and breaks a centralized solar network; four centuries later, recovery of the buried record begins the second dawn.
chapters.sequenceNote: Its regional scope and four-century internal interval are fixed by authoritative chronology.

chapters.title: Terminal Convergence
chapters.description: After every admitted magic-active material history, the universe reaches its final reckoning.
chapters.sequenceNote: Fixed as the last material-history event before the Long Zero.

chapters.title: The Long Zero
chapters.description: Ages of perfect absence separate extinction from return. The empty space is part of the chronology.
chapters.sequenceNote: Fixed between Terminal Convergence and the Joined-Sky reawakening.

chapters.title: The Joined-Sky Reawakening
chapters.description: Ages after the perfect zero, sky and world remember one another and existence begins again in a transformed register.
chapters.sequenceNote: Fixed as the furthest known point on the shared-universe chronology.
